source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 10 mathematics textbooks (advanced stream)

stages.headline: f increases on an interval if x₁ < x₂ ⇒ f(x₁) < f(x₂), decreases if f(x₁) > f(x₂); y = (x − 1)² − 3 decreases on (−∞; 1] and increases on [1; +∞).
stages.headlineEnglish: f increases on an interval if x₁ < x₂ ⇒ f(x₁) < f(x₂), decreases if f(x₁) > f(x₂); y = (x − 1)² − 3 decreases on (−∞; 1] and increases on [1; +∞).

stages.headline: x₀ is a maximum point if f(x) ≤ f(x₀) near x₀ and a minimum point if f(x) ≥ f(x₀); these are extremum points.
stages.headlineEnglish: x₀ is a maximum point if f(x) ≤ f(x₀) near x₀ and a minimum point if f(x) ≥ f(x₀); these are extremum points.

stages.headline: Example: y = x² − 4x + 3 = (x − 2)² − 1 decreases on (−∞; 2], increases on [2; +∞), has a minimum at x = 2 with value −1.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: y = x² − 4x + 3 = (x − 2)² − 1 decreases on (−∞; 2], increases on [2; +∞), has a minimum at x = 2 with value −1.
